name: Medra
summary: Medra develops an AI and robotics platform intended to design, execute, and interpret experiments for biopharma research.
overview: Medra is building a physical-AI system for scientific research, combining hypothesis generation with robotic experimental execution. It announced a $52 million Series A in December 2025, led by Human Capital, without disclosing a valuation.

facts.label: Latest financing
facts.note: Medra announced a $52 million Series A; its valuation was not disclosed.

bull_case: Closed-loop experimentation can make AI more useful in drug discovery if Medra's systems produce reliable results inside real lab workflows.
bear_case: Biopharma adoption requires rigorous validation, integration into laboratory operations, and a credible path through hardware complexity.
directory_notes: Public financing and operating data remain limited.

intelligence.description: Physical AI for hypothesis generation, robotic experiments, and biopharma research workflows.

metrics.label: Latest valuation
metrics.note: Valuation was not announced with the Series A

company: Medra is building a Physical AI Scientist that combines scientific reasoning with general-purpose robots that can execute experiments. The company says the system is designed to run a tighter loop between designing, conducting, and interpreting laboratory work.

In December 2025, Medra announced a $52 million Series A led by Human Capital. It named Genentech, Cultivarium, and Addition Therapeutics as early biopharma partners, while the funding announcement did not disclose a valuation.
intelligence.why_it_matters: Drug discovery is a high-value application for AI, but the bottleneck often remains physical experimental work. Medra is a private-market bet on bringing model-driven workflows directly into laboratory execution.

changed.text: Medra announced a $52M Series A led by Human Capital.

takeaways: The December 2025 Series A is the latest disclosed funding event.
Biopharma partnerships are the key evidence point for commercial validation.
Laboratory reliability and integration are the central execution risks.
